title: The job changes the score
hook: A toy product serves two tasks. Does its average score survive a context shift?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Condition an offer’s expected fit on the explicit task mix rather than on its attributes alone.

misconception: A product has one context-free value that ranks it for every task.
objective: Condition an offer’s expected fit on the explicit task mix rather than on its attributes alone.

claims.text: Original stipulated payoff model: A inputs [20, 18, 2] yield 5.2; B inputs [80, 18, 2] yield 14.8. Prediction correct option 14.8. A scores {A}; B scores {B}. The product is unchanged; its 18-point fit matters more when task X occurs four times as often. Task frequencies and fit points are stipulated, not measured preferences or a choice law.

claims.text: A toy tool scores 14 on task X and 4 on task Y; each occurs half the time. Expected fit? 0.5 × 14 + 0.5 × 4 = 9; the fit is conditional on the stipulated task mix.
